structured_output.hypothesis: If the Glacial period was at least partly simultaneous across the whole world, the globally distributed benthic d18O stack must show long-lived (tens of thousands of years) high-d18O glacial states, and the 57 contributing records from different basins and hemispheres must be coherent enough to produce a stack with a small error band at those times.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In the LR04 stack (Appendix 1), d18O stays above the 0-800 ka mean for a continuous interval of at least 10 kyr in at least 7 of the last 8 glacial cycles (MIS 2, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18), and the stack's reported standard error during those intervals is below 0.1 per mil, which is under 10% of the glacial-interglacial amplitude of about 1.5 per mil. Both conditions must hold.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Claim refuted if fewer than 5 of the 8 glacial cycles show a continuous above-mean interval of at least 10 kyr, or if the stack's standard error during glacial intervals exceeds 0.3 per mil (more than 20% of the amplitude), which would mean the contributing records are not coherent.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'Glacial period' is mapped to Pleistocene glacial stages, i.e. intervals of high benthic foraminiferal d18O, which record mainly global ice volume plus deep-water temperature. 'Simultaneous across the whole world' is mapped to coherence of globally distributed records within the age-model uncertainty (about 4 kyr in LR04). Modern reinterpretation: the Pleistocene had many glacial cycles, not one period. d18O is a proxy for ice volume and deep-ocean temperature, not a direct surface-air temperature record. LR04 ages are orbitally tuned, so synchrony is partly built in, and the stack alone cannot resolve hemispheric lead/lag. The test therefore decides only the 'global cooling at the same time' reading, not the stronger hemispheric-synchrony reading, and this limitation is stated up front.

dataset.name: Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of globally distributed benthic stable oxygen isotope records
dataset.why_it_fits: The landing page offers a ZIP of tab-delimited files. Appendix 1 (10.1594/PANGAEA.701576) is the global stack, with age in ka, d18O and its error. Fields used: age, d18O, standard error. The stack averages 57 benthic records from across the global ocean, so it directly measures whether glacial states were shared worldwide and how long they lasted.
